citation.title: A complete Physics-Informed Neural Network-based framework for structural topology optimization
citation.authors: Hyogu Jeong, Chanaka Batuwatta-Gamage, Jinshuai Bai, Yi Min Xie, Charith Rathnayaka, Ying Zhou, YuanTong Gu
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
citation.version_coded: version of record, open institutional repository copy

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the three-dimensional examples, the PINN framework needed less than half as many optimization iterations as SIMP to obtain a design.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Separate 2D comparison, Table 2 case (a): 53.95 s SIMP / 16,872 s CPINNTO = 0.003197 [inferred]; the primary 3D iteration claim has no wall-time ratio. The article describes CPINNTO as at least 312 times slower than SIMP in 2D.
claim.alternatives: Section 4.1/Table 1 reports fewer iterations but slightly worse quality versus projected SIMP. Section 4.1/Table 2 reports CPINNTO wall time at least 312 times longer than ordinary SIMP and 34 times longer than projected SIMP. Abstract emphasizes comparable quality.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP, with and without Heaviside projection (Section 4.1); 3D SIMP (Section 4.6)
baseline.implementation: MATLAB 88-line code by Andreassen et al. for 2D (Section 4.1); MATLAB code by Liu and Tovar for 3D (Section 4.6)
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel Core i7-10700 CPU @ 2.90 GHz, 16.0 GB DDR4 RAM (Section 4)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Core i7-10700 CPU @ 2.90 GHz, 16.0 GB DDR4 RAM (Section 4)
baseline.problem_size: 80 x 40 elements for 2D validation (Section 4.1); 40 x 20 x 20 and 60 x 20 x 10 hexahedra for 3D (Section 4.6)
baseline.classical_iterations: 2D case (a): 154 SIMP or 1,394 with Heaviside; 3D counts only plotted (Table 1; Figure 19)
baseline.classical_time: 2D case (a): 53.95 s SIMP or 492.63 s with Heaviside (Table 2); 3D not stated
baseline.training_time: No offline training; two PINNs are trained per problem and their time is within the reported run time (Sections 3-4)
baseline.data_generation_cost: No labeled training data required (abstract; Section 5)
baseline.quality_metric: Compliance recalculated in the 88-line FEA code for 2D and evaluated with COMSOL for 3D; target volume fractions (Sections 4.1 and 4.6)
baseline.quality_gap: 2D projected SIMP case (a) compliance objective 5.3741 versus CPINNTO 5.5382, a stated 3.05% gap (Table 1); 3D up to 6% lower for cantilever and 8% higher for bridge with CPINNTO (Section 4.6)

R1.evidence: Conclusion claims fewer 3D iterations as an efficiency proxy; Section 4.6 reports one PINN bridge design has 8% higher compliance and no matching at equal quality or time. Section 4.1/Table 2 shows the PINN takes far longer in 2D.

R2.evidence: Sections 4 and 4.1 identify matched CPU hardware and a standard SIMP implementation; no R2(a)-(e) condition is established.

R3.evidence: Abstract and Sections 3-4: the two PINNs train for each optimization problem without labeled data; their training time is part of the optimization run.

R4.evidence: Section 4.1 imports returned designs into the 88-line FEA code, and Section 4.6 evaluates 3D designs in COMSOL; target volumes are stated, but failed or infeasible design rates are not reported. Section 5 acknowledges some irrational designs.

reporting.n_test_cases: 4 standard 2D validation cases (Table 1) and 2 3D cases (Section 4.6), plus other variations

notes: The conclusion's first quantitative classical comparison is an iteration-count claim, which determines the speed stratum despite the paper's explicit opposite wall-time result. Training is intrinsic to each design.
